content.summary: In this reading mission, you will read a short story about students in a library. They ask for permission, request help, and offer help in a polite way. Look for the useful phrases "May I", "Could you", and "Shall I". These phrases help people sound kind and respectful.

linguisticTarget.grammar: May I + base verb for permission; Could you + base verb for polite requests; Shall I + base verb for offers of help.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words for borrowing, lending, carrying, help, permission, and polite replies.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: First, skim the passage to understand the main situation. Then, scan for names, objects, and polite phrases to find key details.

contextWarmup.prompt: You want to use your friend's pen. Which sentence is the most polite?
options: May I borrow your pen, please?
contextWarmup.explanation: "May I borrow your pen, please?" is polite because it asks for permission. The word "please" also makes the request friendlier.

rules: Use "Could you + base verb" to ask another person for help politely: "Could you help me, please?"
Use "May I + base verb" to ask for permission: "May I borrow your pen?"
Use "Shall I + base verb" to offer help: "Shall I carry the box for you?"

commonTrap.explanation: Do not confuse asking for permission with offering help. "May I" asks if you can do something. "Shall I" asks if the other person wants your help.

sections.title: Reading Passage: A Helpful Morning at the Library

content.passageTitle: A Helpful Morning at the Library
content.context: Mia and Leo are in the school library. Read how they use polite language to ask for help, ask permission, and offer help.
content.text:
On Monday morning, Mia is in the school library. She needs a blue pen for her homework form. Her friend Leo is reading near the window. Mia says, "Excuse me, Leo. May I borrow your blue pen, please?" Leo smiles and says, "Of course. Here you are." Mia thanks him.

A few minutes later, Leo has a box of new books. The box is heavy. Mia says, "Shall I carry the box for you?" "Yes, please. That would be very helpful," says Leo.

At the desk, the librarian is speaking to a teacher. Mia waits. Then she says, "Sorry to interrupt. Could you help me find a book about animals?" The librarian points to a shelf. "Certainly," she says. Mia finds the book and returns Leo's pen. "Thank you for your help," she says.

sections.title: Audio Dialogue: Help at the Office

content.context: Emma is working in her office and needs help with a report. She asks her colleague Daniel for help and permission to borrow his pen. Later, Emma offers to carry Daniel's files and bring his laptop.
content.audioPrompt: Listen carefully to the following dialogue between two colleagues in an office.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Good morning, Daniel. Could you help me with this report, please? I'm having trouble with the numbers.
lines.translation: Selamat pagi, Daniel. Bisakah kamu membantu saya dengan laporan ini? Saya kesulitan dengan angka-angkanya.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Of course, Emma. I'd be happy to help. What seems to be the problem?
lines.translation: Tentu saja, Emma. Saya dengan senang hati membantu. Apa masalahnya?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Thank you so much! Also, may I borrow your blue pen? Mine has run out of ink.
lines.translation: Terima kasih banyak! Juga, bolehkah saya meminjam pulpen biru Anda? Pulpen saya kehabisan tinta.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yes, certainly. Here you are. You can keep it until tomorrow if you need to.
lines.translation: Ya, tentu. Ini dia. Kamu bisa memakainya sampai besok kalau perlu.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: That's very kind of you. Oh, you have a lot of files there. Shall I help you carry them to the meeting room?
lines.translation: Kamu baik sekali. Oh, kamu punya banyak file di sana. Haruskah saya membantu membawanya ke ruang rapat?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That would be great, thank you! They're quite heavy.
lines.translation: Itu akan sangat membantu, terima kasih! Mereka cukup berat.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: No problem at all. Shall I also bring the laptop for the presentation?
lines.translation: Tidak masalah sama sekali. Haruskah saya juga membawa laptop untuk presentasi?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: No, thank you. I already have it in my bag. But I really appreciate your help with the files!
lines.translation: Tidak, terima kasih. Saya sudah menaruhnya di tas saya. Tapi saya sangat menghargai bantuan Anda dengan file-file ini!

content.summary: Use polite phrases when you ask for help, ask for permission, or offer help. Start with Could you, May I, or Shall I. Use a question mark at the end of each question.

mechanicsRules.rule: Begin every sentence with a capital letter.
mechanicsRules.why: The first word in a sentence needs a capital letter.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a question mark after a polite question.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Could you close the door please.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Could you close the door, please?
mechanicsRules.why: Could you, May I, and Shall I sentences are questions.

mechanicsRules.rule: Write I with a capital letter.
mechanicsRules.why: The word I is always a capital letter in English.

Shall I help you with your homework?
Yes, please. That would be nice.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Polite Requests, Permission & Offers

content.summary: Use polite, calm language when you ask for help, ask for permission, or offer help. Say Could you...?, May I...?, and Shall I...? clearly. Speak at a slow speed and use a friendly voice.
content.audioGuidance: Stress the important action words, such as use, help, borrow, show, and carry. Use rising intonation for polite yes-or-no questions: May I use the computer? Use a warm, helpful tone for offers: Shall I help you? Pause before please and thank you.

pillars.name: Polite Request
pillars.explanation: Use Could you to ask another person for help. For example: Could you help me find a book, please?

pillars.name: Permission
pillars.explanation: Use May I to ask politely if something is allowed. For example: May I use this computer?

pillars.name: Helpful Offer
pillars.explanation: Use Shall I to offer help. For example: Shall I show you the history section?

pillars.name: Friendly Intonation
pillars.explanation: Let your voice rise gently at the end of a polite question. This makes your question sound friendly and respectful.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: PERmit is a noun, meaning official permission. PerMIT is a verb, meaning to allow. The stress changes the word type.
A PREsent is a gift. To preSENT means to show or give something formally, such as a student card.

drills.targetText: May I use the computer, please?
drills.hint: Stress use and computer. Let your voice rise slightly on please.

drills.targetText: Could you help me find this book?
drills.phonetic: /kʊd juː help miː faɪnd ðɪs bʊk/
drills.hint: Link could and you smoothly: could-you. Stress help, find, and book.

drills.targetText: Shall I show you the history section?
drills.phonetic: /ʃæl aɪ ʃəʊ juː ðə ˈhɪstəri ˈsekʃən/
drills.hint: Say shall I as one smooth group. Use a warm rising tone at the end.

drills.targetText: May I borrow five books for two weeks?
drills.phonetic: /meɪ aɪ ˈbɒrəʊ faɪv bʊks fə tuː wiːks/

drills.targetText: No, thank you. That is very kind.
drills.phonetic: /nəʊ θæŋk juː ðæt ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd/
drills.hint: Say thank you warmly. Use a gentle falling tone at the end because this is a statement.

roleplay.context: You are in a university library. Mr. Khoirul is a friendly librarian. Ask for permission, request help, and respond politely to an offer.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Good afternoon! Welcome to the library. How can I help you today?
turns.translation: Selamat siang! Selamat datang di perpustakaan. Bagaimana saya bisa membantu Anda hari ini?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Good afternoon! May I use the computer in the corner for my research?
turns.translation: Selamat siang! Bolehkah saya menggunakan komputer di sudut untuk penelitian saya?

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Yes, of course. You can use it for up to two hours. Do you have your student card with you?
turns.translation: Ya, tentu saja. Anda dapat menggunakannya sampai dua jam. Apakah Anda membawa kartu mahasiswa?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, I do. Here it is. Could you also help me find books about British history, please?
turns.translation: Ya, saya bawa. Ini kartunya. Bisakah Anda juga membantu saya menemukan buku tentang sejarah Inggris, tolong?

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Certainly! The history section is on the second floor. I have to take some books there anyway. Shall I show you where it is?
turns.translation: Tentu! Bagian sejarah ada di lantai dua. Saya juga harus membawa beberapa buku ke sana. Haruskah saya menunjukkan tempatnya?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: That would be wonderful, thank you! Also, may I borrow up to five books at a time?
turns.translation: Itu akan sangat bagus, terima kasih! Selain itu, bolehkah saya meminjam sampai lima buku sekaligus?

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Yes, students can borrow up to five books for two weeks. You are carrying a lot of things. Shall I help you carry your backpack upstairs?
turns.translation: Ya, mahasiswa dapat meminjam sampai lima buku selama dua minggu. Anda membawa banyak barang. Haruskah saya membantu membawa ransel Anda ke atas?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: No, thank you. That is very kind, but I can manage. I really appreciate all your help today!
turns.translation: Tidak, terima kasih. Anda sangat baik, tetapi saya bisa membawanya sendiri. Saya sangat menghargai semua bantuan Anda hari ini!
